Others said: The smoke has not yet passed; rather it is one of the signs of the Hour, as has preceded in the hadith of Abu Surayhah Hudhayfah ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked down upon us from a upper room while we were discussing the Hour, and he said: "The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from its west, the smoke, the beast, the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, the descent of 'Isa ibn Maryam, the Dajjal, and three eclipses: an eclipse in the east, an eclipse in the west, and an eclipse in the Arabian Peninsula, and a fire that will come out from the bottom of Aden, driving the people [or: gathering the people]: it will spend the night with them wherever they spend the night, and take a rest with them wherever they rest." Muslim alone recorded it in his Sahih. [Sahih Muslim no. 2901.]

In the Two Sahihs, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ibn al-Sayyad: "I have hidden something for you." He said: "It is the smoke (al-dukh)." So he said to him: "Be humiliated! You will not exceed your measure." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had hidden for him: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke﴾. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3055 and Sahih Muslim no. 2930, from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]

This indicates that it is among the awaited and expected things. Ibn al-Sayyad was a soothsayer in the manner of the diviners, speaking through the tongue of the jinn, and they would conceal the expression; therefore he said: "It is the dukh," meaning the dukhan (smoke). Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recognized its source, that it was satanic, so he said to him: "Be humiliated! You will not exceed your measure."

Then Ibn Jarir said: Isam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah narrated to me, my father narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri narrated to us, Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from Ribi ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say: [Variant: "And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Hudhayfah, who said:"] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of the signs is the Dajjal, the descent of 'Isa ibn Maryam, and a fire that comes out from the bottom of Aden, the most distant, driving the people to the place of gathering; it rests with them when they rest, and it takes its nap with them when they nap; and the smoke." Hudhayfah said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the smoke? Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke, covering the people. This is a painful punishment﴾, "it fills what is between the east and the west, remaining for forty days and nights. As for the believer, it affects him like a cold (zukmah), and as for the disbeliever, it will be like a drunkard, coming out from his nostrils, his ears, and his anus." [Tafsir al-Tabari 25/68; it was also narrated by al-Tha'labi in his Tafsir, as in Takhrij Ahadith al-Kashshaf by al-Zayla'i no. 1174, and by al-Baghawi in Ma'alim al-Tanzil 7/230.]

Ibn Jarir said: If this hadith were sound, it would be decisive, but I do not testify to its soundness, because Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told me that he asked Rawwad about this hadith: "Did he hear it from Sufyan?" He said: "No." He said: "I said: Did you read it to him?" He said: "No." I said to him: "Was it read to him while you were present, and he confirmed it?" He said: "No." I said to him: "Then where did you get it from?" He said: "A group of people brought it to me and presented it to me, and they said to me: 'Listen to it from us.' They read it to me, then they went off with it and narrated it from me, or as he said."

Ibn Jarir has indeed done well in this place, for this hadith is fabricated (mawdu') with this chain. Ibn Jarir frequently cited it in several places of this Tafsir, and it contains very many rejected reports (munkarat), especially at the beginning of Surat Bani Isra'il in mentioning the Farthest Mosque (al-Masjid al-Aqsa). And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Safwan narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, Khalil narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: "The smoke will spread among the people. As for the believer, it will seize him like a cold, and as for the disbeliever, it will inflate him until it comes out from every opening of his." [Note: the Arabic phrase "من كل مسمع منه"]

It was narrated by Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri as a mawquf (stopping at the Companion). And Awf narrated it from al-Hasan as his own statement.

Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn Awf narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'ah narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed your Lord has warned you of three things: the smoke, which will seize the believer like a cold and will seize the disbeliever so that he swells until it comes out from every opening of his. The second is the beast, and the third is the Dajjal." [Variant: "Dammam" in one copy.]

Al-Tabarani narrated it from Hashim ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash, with the same chain. [Tafsir al-Tabari 25/68 and al-Mu'jam al-Kabir 3/292. The statement of al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir here, "this is a good chain" (isnad jayyid), is open to challenge, for this version has three defects: First: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash. Abu Hatim said: "He did not hear anything from his father; they made him narrate, so he narrated." Second: Dammam ibn Zur'ah. Abu Hatim weakened him, and Ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy (thiqah); and Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash, Abu Dawud said: "He was not of that standard." Third: Shurayh ibn Ubayd, whose hearing from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari has been questioned. Abu Hatim said: "Shurayh ibn Ubayd from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari is mursal (has a missing link)."]

This is a good chain (isnad jayyid).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Salih ibn Muslim narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The verse of the smoke has not yet passed. It will seize the believer like the form of a cold, and it will inflate the disbeliever until it passes through."

Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of al-Walid ibn Jumay', from Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughirah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Baylamani, from Ibn Umar, who said: "The smoke will come out and seize the believer like the form of a cold, and it will enter the ears of the disbeliever and the hypocrite until he becomes like a roasted head (ra's al-hanidh), that is, roasted on hot stones (al-radf)."

Then Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to me, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, [Variant: "And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain"] from Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: I went to Ibn Abbas one day, and he said: "I did not sleep last night until morning." I said: "Why?" He said: "They said the star with the tail (al-kawkab dhu al-dhanab) has risen, and I feared that the smoke had come by night, so I did not sleep until morning." [Tafsir al-Tabari 25/68.] Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in this same form from his father, from Ibn Umar, from Sufyan, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn Abbas, as mentioned. [Variant: "Ibn Jarir narrated it in this form, from Ibn Abi Hatim, from his father..."] This chain is sound (sahih) up to Ibn Abbas, the scholar of the Ummah (habr al-ummah) and the interpreter of the Qur'an (turjuman al-Qur'an). This is also the view of all those among the Companions and Successors who agreed with him, together with the raised (marfu') hadiths from the sound and fair (hisan) collections and others, which we have cited, and which provide sufficient proof and clear indication that the smoke is one of the awaited signs, while it is also the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke﴾, that is, clear and evident, which everyone sees. As for what Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, explained: it is only an imagining they saw in their eyes from the intensity of hunger and hardship. Similarly His saying: ﴿covering the people﴾, that is, it envelops them and overwhelms them; and if it were an imagined matter specific to the polytheists of Makkah, it would not have been said: ﴿covering the people﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿This is a painful punishment﴾, that is, it will be said to them as a rebuke and reproach, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The Day they will be pushed into the Fire of Hell with a violent push: "This is the Fire which you used to deny."﴾ [al-Tur 52:13–14], or some of them will say it to others.

* *

Their saying: "Our Lord, remove the punishment from us; indeed we are believers" (Qur'an 44:12). That is, the disbelievers, when they witness Allah's punishment and retribution, will say, seeking its lifting and removal from them, like His saying: "If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire, and they say, 'Would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers'" (Qur'an 6:27). Likewise His saying: "And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, 'Our Lord, delay us for a brief term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.' Did you not previously swear that for you there would be no decline?" (Qur'an 14:44). And so He says here: "How will they have the reminder, when there has come to them a clear messenger, and then they turned away from him and said, 'A taught one, a madman'" (Qur'an 44:13–14).

He says: How can they have remembrance, when We have sent to them a messenger clear in the message and the warning, and yet they turned away from him and did not agree with him, but rather denied him and said, "A taught one, a madman." This is like His saying, exalted is He: "On that Day man will remember, but how will the remembrance benefit him? He will say, 'Oh, would that I had sent ahead for my life'" (Qur'an 89:23–24). And His saying, exalted is He: "If only you could see when they are terrified and there is no escape, and they are seized from a near place. And they say, 'We believe in Him.' But how can they reach [faith] from a distant place? And they had disbelieved in it before, and they hurl [accusations] about the unseen from a distant place. And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as was done with their counterparts before; indeed they were in disquieting doubt" (Qur'an 34:51–54).

* *

His saying: "Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little; indeed you will return" (Qur'an 44:15) admits of two meanings:

The first: that Allah says, "Even if We removed the punishment from you and returned you to the worldly abode, you would return to what you were in of disbelief and denial," like His saying: "Even if We had mercy upon them and removed what harm is upon them, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly" (Qur'an 23:75), and like His saying: "And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars" (Qur'an 6:28).

The second: that the intended meaning is: "We will delay the punishment from you a little after its causes have been established and it has reached you, while you remain persisting in what you are in of rebellion and misguidance." Removing it from them does not necessarily mean that it has touched them, like His saying, exalted is He: "Except the people of Yunus; when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and We gave them enjoyment for a time" (Qur'an 10:98). The punishment had not touched them and reached them, but its cause had been established upon them. Nor does it necessarily follow that they had ceased from their disbelief and then returned to it. Allah, exalted is He, related about Shu'ayb that he said to his people when they said: "We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you, from our town, or you will return to our religion." He said: "Even if we were unwilling? We would have fabricated a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion after Allah has delivered us from it" (Qur'an 7:88–89). Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, had never been upon their religion and way.

Qatadah said: "Indeed you will return" means to the punishment of Allah.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: "The Day We will seize with the greatest seizing; indeed We will take retribution" (Qur'an 44:16). Ibn Mas'ud interpreted that as the Day of Badr. This is the view of a group who agreed with Ibn Mas'ud's interpretation of the smoke as explained earlier. It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas [and a group] through the narration of al-'Awfi from him, and from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and a group, and it is possible.

The apparent meaning is that it is the Day of Resurrection, although the Day of Badr was also a day of seizing.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub related to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, Khalid al-Hadhdha' related to us, from 'Ikrimah who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "The greatest seizing is the Day of Badr," and I say: it is the Day of Resurrection.

This is a sound chain from him, and al-Hasan al-Basri and 'Ikrimah in the more correct of the two reports from him, hold this view.

He, the Exalted, says: Rather, these polytheists are in doubt, playing about. That is, the certainty (al-yaqin) has come to them, [Variant in another manuscript: "al-mubin" (the clear)], yet they doubt it, dispute it, and do not believe in it. Then He said, threatening and warning them: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke﴾.

Al-A'mash, Sulayman ibn Mihran, narrated from Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subayh, [Variant in another copy: "Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it in their Sahihs."] from Masruq, who said: We entered the mosque, meaning the Mosque of Kufa, at the gates of Kindah, and there was a man telling a story to his companions: ﴿On the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke﴾. "Do you know what that smoke is? It is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection, seizing the hearing and sight of the hypocrites, while the believers will be affected by it like a cold (zukam)." Masruq said: We came to Ibn Mas'ud and mentioned that to him. He was lying down, so he sprang up and sat, and said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to your Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it, and I am not of those who pretend﴾ [Sad 38:86]. Indeed, part of knowledge is that a man says, regarding what he does not know, 'Allah knows best.' I will tell you about this. When Quraysh were slow to accept Islam and defied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he invoked against them with years like the years of Yusuf. They were struck by hardship and hunger until they ate bones and carrion, and they kept raising their eyes to the sky and seeing nothing but smoke." [In another narration: "A man would look at the sky and see between himself and it something like smoke, from the hardship."] He said: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke, covering the people. This is a painful punishment﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to him and it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to give rain to Mudar, for they have perished." So he asked for rain for them, and they were given rain. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed We will remove the punishment a little; indeed you will return﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: "So the punishment will be removed from them on the Day of Resurrection [i.e., the earlier one, and when they were given ease, they returned to their state]. Then Allah revealed: ﴿The Day We will seize with the greatest seizing; indeed We will take vengeance﴾." He said: That means the Day of Badr.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Five have already passed: the smoke, the Romans, the moon, the seizing, and the lasting punishment (al-lizam)." This hadith is recorded in the Two Sahihs. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4820 and Sahih Muslim no. 2798.] Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, and it is found in al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in their Tafsirs [Variant: "tafsirayhima"]. It is also found in Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim through multiple chains from al-A'mash, with the same wording. [Musnad 1/380, 431; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3254; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 11481; Tafsir al-Tabari 25/66.]

A group of the early scholars (al-salaf) agreed with Ibn Mas'ud's interpretation of this verse, and that the smoke has already passed, such as Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, and Atiyyah al-Awfi. This is also the view chosen by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Musafir narrated to us, Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, [Variant: "And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain from"] Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, regarding His saying: ﴿On the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke﴾, that it was the Day of the Conquest of Makkah.

Muslim alone recorded it in his Sahih. [Sahih Muslim no. 2901.]

In the Two Sahihs, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ibn al-Sayyad: "I have hidden something for you." He said: "It is the smoke (al-dukh)." So he said to him: "Be humiliated! You will not exceed your measure." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had hidden for him: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke﴾. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3055 and Sahih Muslim no. 2930, from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]

He said: "No." I said to him: "Then where did you get it from?" He said: "A group of people brought it to me and presented it to me, and they said to me: 'Listen to it from us.' They read it to me, then they went off with it and narrated it from me, or as he said."

* *

That is, the disbelievers, when they witness Allah's punishment and retribution, will say, seeking its lifting and removal from them, like His saying: "If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire, and they say, 'Would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers'" (Qur'an 6:27). Likewise His saying: "And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, 'Our Lord, delay us for a brief term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.' Did you not previously swear that for you there would be no decline?" (Qur'an 14:44). And so He says here: "How will they have the reminder, when there has come to them a clear messenger, and then they turned away from him and said, 'A taught one, a madman'" (Qur'an 44:13–14).

He says: How can they have remembrance, when We have sent to them a messenger clear in the message and the warning, and yet they turned away from him and did not agree with him, but rather denied him and said, "A taught one, a madman." This is like His saying, exalted is He: "On that Day man will remember, but how will the remembrance benefit him? He will say, 'Oh, would that I had sent ahead for my life'" (Qur'an 89:23–24). And His saying, exalted is He: "If only you could see when they are terrified and there is no escape, and they are seized from a near place. And they say, 'We believe in Him.' But how can they reach [faith] from a distant place? And they had disbelieved in it before, and they hurl [accusations] about the unseen from a distant place. And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as was done with their counterparts before; indeed they were in disquieting doubt" (Qur'an 34:51–54).

* *

His saying: "Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little; indeed you will return" (Qur'an 44:15) admits of two meanings:

The first: that Allah says, "Even if We removed the punishment from you and returned you to the worldly abode, you would return to what you were in of disbelief and denial," like His saying: "Even if We had mercy upon them and removed what harm is upon them, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly" (Qur'an 23:75), and like His saying: "And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars" (Qur'an 6:28).

The second: that the intended meaning is: "We will delay the punishment from you a little after its causes have been established and it has reached you, while you remain persisting in what you are in of rebellion and misguidance." Removing it from them does not necessarily mean that it has touched them, like His saying, exalted is He: "Except the people of Yunus; when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and We gave them enjoyment for a time" (Qur'an 10:98). The punishment had not touched them and reached them, but its cause had been established upon them. Nor does it necessarily follow that they had ceased from their disbelief and then returned to it. Allah, exalted is He, related about Shu'ayb that he said to his people when they said: "We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you, from our town, or you will return to our religion." He said: "Even if we were unwilling? We would have fabricated a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion after Allah has delivered us from it" (Qur'an 7:88–89). Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, had never been upon their religion and way.

Qatadah said: "Indeed you will return" means to the punishment of Allah.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: "The Day We will seize with the greatest seizing; indeed We will take retribution" (Qur'an 44:16). Ibn Mas'ud interpreted that as the Day of Badr. This is the view of a group who agreed with Ibn Mas'ud's interpretation of the smoke as explained earlier. It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas [and a group] through the narration of al-'Awfi from him, and from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and a group, and it is possible.

The apparent meaning is that it is the Day of Resurrection, although the Day of Badr was also a day of seizing.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub related to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, Khalid al-Hadhdha' related to us, from 'Ikrimah who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "The greatest seizing is the Day of Badr," and I say: it is the Day of Resurrection.

This is a sound chain from him, and al-Hasan al-Basri and 'Ikrimah in the more correct of the two reports from him, hold this view.

He, the Exalted, says: Rather, these polytheists are in doubt, playing about. That is, the certainty (al-yaqin) has come to them, [Variant in another manuscript: "al-mubin" (the clear)], yet they doubt it, dispute it, and do not believe in it. Then He said, threatening and warning them: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke﴾.

Al-A'mash, Sulayman ibn Mihran, narrated from Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subayh, [Variant in another copy: "Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it in their Sahihs."] from Masruq, who said: We entered the mosque, meaning the Mosque of Kufa, at the gates of Kindah, and there was a man telling a story to his companions: ﴿On the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke﴾. "Do you know what that smoke is? It is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection, seizing the hearing and sight of the hypocrites, while the believers will be affected by it like a cold (zukam)." Masruq said: We came to Ibn Mas'ud and mentioned that to him. He was lying down, so he sprang up and sat, and said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to your Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it, and I am not of those who pretend﴾ [Sad 38:86]. Indeed, part of knowledge is that a man says, regarding what he does not know, 'Allah knows best.' I will tell you about this. When Quraysh were slow to accept Islam and defied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he invoked against them with years like the years of Yusuf. They were struck by hardship and hunger until they ate bones and carrion, and they kept raising their eyes to the sky and seeing nothing but smoke." [In another narration: "A man would look at the sky and see between himself and it something like smoke, from the hardship."] He said: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke, covering the people. This is a painful punishment﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to him and it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to give rain to Mudar, for they have perished." So he asked for rain for them, and they were given rain. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed We will remove the punishment a little; indeed you will return﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: "So the punishment will be removed from them on the Day of Resurrection [i.e., the earlier one, and when they were given ease, they returned to their state]. Then Allah revealed: ﴿The Day We will seize with the greatest seizing; indeed We will take vengeance﴾." He said: That means the Day of Badr.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Five have already passed: the smoke, the Romans, the moon, the seizing, and the lasting punishment (al-lizam)." This hadith is recorded in the Two Sahihs. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4820 and Sahih Muslim no. 2798.] Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, and it is found in al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in their Tafsirs [Variant: "tafsirayhima"]. It is also found in Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim through multiple chains from al-A'mash, with the same wording. [Musnad 1/380, 431; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3254; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 11481; Tafsir al-Tabari 25/66.]

A group of the early scholars (al-salaf) agreed with Ibn Mas'ud's interpretation of this verse, and that the smoke has already passed, such as Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, and Atiyyah al-Awfi. This is also the view chosen by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Musafir narrated to us, Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, [Variant: "And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain from"] Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, regarding His saying: ﴿On the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke﴾, that it was the Day of the Conquest of Makkah.

This view is extremely strange (gharib), indeed rejected (munkar).

Others said: The smoke has not yet passed; rather it is one of the signs of the Hour, as has preceded in the hadith of Abu Surayhah Hudhayfah ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked down upon us from a upper room while we were discussing the Hour, and he said: "The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from its west, the smoke, the beast, the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, the descent of 'Isa ibn Maryam, the Dajjal, and three eclipses: an eclipse in the east, an eclipse in the west, and an eclipse in the Arabian Peninsula, and a fire that will come out from the bottom of Aden, driving the people [or: gathering the people]: it will spend the night with them wherever they spend the night, and take a rest with them wherever they rest." Muslim alone recorded it in his Sahih. [Sahih Muslim no. 2901.]

In the Two Sahihs, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ibn al-Sayyad: "I have hidden something for you." He said: "It is the smoke (al-dukh)." So he said to him: "Be humiliated! You will not exceed your measure." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had hidden for him: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke﴾. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3055 and Sahih Muslim no. 2930, from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]

This indicates that it is among the awaited and expected things. Ibn al-Sayyad was a soothsayer in the manner of the diviners, speaking through the tongue of the jinn, and they would conceal the expression; therefore he said: "It is the dukh," meaning the dukhan (smoke). Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recognized its source, that it was satanic, so he said to him: "Be humiliated! You will not exceed your measure."

Then Ibn Jarir said: Isam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah narrated to me, my father narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri narrated to us, Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from Ribi ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say: [Variant: "And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Hudhayfah, who said:"] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of the signs is the Dajjal, the descent of 'Isa ibn Maryam, and a fire that comes out from the bottom of Aden, the most distant, driving the people to the place of gathering; it rests with them when they rest, and it takes its nap with them when they nap; and the smoke." Hudhayfah said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the smoke? Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke, covering the people. This is a painful punishment﴾, "it fills what is between the east and the west, remaining for forty days and nights. As for the believer, it affects him like a cold (zukmah), and as for the disbeliever, it will be like a drunkard, coming out from his nostrils, his ears, and his anus." [Tafsir al-Tabari 25/68; it was also narrated by al-Tha'labi in his Tafsir, as in Takhrij Ahadith al-Kashshaf by al-Zayla'i no. 1174, and by al-Baghawi in Ma'alim al-Tanzil 7/230.]

Ibn Jarir said: If this hadith were sound, it would be decisive, but I do not testify to its soundness, because Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told me that he asked Rawwad about this hadith: "Did he hear it from Sufyan?" He said: "No." He said: "I said: Did you read it to him?" He said: "No." I said to him: "Was it read to him while you were present, and he confirmed it?" He said: "No." I said to him: "Then where did you get it from?" He said: "A group of people brought it to me and presented it to me, and they said to me: 'Listen to it from us.' They read it to me, then they went off with it and narrated it from me, or as he said."

Ibn Jarir has indeed done well in this place, for this hadith is fabricated (mawdu') with this chain. Ibn Jarir frequently cited it in several places of this Tafsir, and it contains very many rejected reports (munkarat), especially at the beginning of Surat Bani Isra'il in mentioning the Farthest Mosque (al-Masjid al-Aqsa). And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Safwan narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, Khalil narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: "The smoke will spread among the people. As for the believer, it will seize him like a cold, and as for the disbeliever, it will inflate him until it comes out from every opening of his." [Note: the Arabic phrase "من كل مسمع منه"]

It was narrated by Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri as a mawquf (stopping at the Companion). And Awf narrated it from al-Hasan as his own statement.

Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn Awf narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'ah narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed your Lord has warned you of three things: the smoke, which will seize the believer like a cold and will seize the disbeliever so that he swells until it comes out from every opening of his. The second is the beast, and the third is the Dajjal." [Variant: "Dammam" in one copy.]

Al-Tabarani narrated it from Hashim ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash, with the same chain. [Tafsir al-Tabari 25/68 and al-Mu'jam al-Kabir 3/292. The statement of al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir here, "this is a good chain" (isnad jayyid), is open to challenge, for this version has three defects: First: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash. Abu Hatim said: "He did not hear anything from his father; they made him narrate, so he narrated." Second: Dammam ibn Zur'ah. Abu Hatim weakened him, and Ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy (thiqah); and Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash, Abu Dawud said: "He was not of that standard." Third: Shurayh ibn Ubayd, whose hearing from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari has been questioned. Abu Hatim said: "Shurayh ibn Ubayd from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari is mursal (has a missing link)."]

This is a good chain (isnad jayyid).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Salih ibn Muslim narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The verse of the smoke has not yet passed. It will seize the believer like the form of a cold, and it will inflate the disbeliever until it passes through."

Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of al-Walid ibn Jumay', from Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughirah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Baylamani, from Ibn Umar, who said: "The smoke will come out and seize the believer like the form of a cold, and it will enter the ears of the disbeliever and the hypocrite until he becomes like a roasted head (ra's al-hanidh), that is, roasted on hot stones (al-radf)."

Then Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to me, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, [Variant: "And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain"] from Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: I went to Ibn Abbas one day, and he said: "I did not sleep last night until morning." I said: "Why?" He said: "They said the star with the tail (al-kawkab dhu al-dhanab) has risen, and I feared that the smoke had come by night, so I did not sleep until morning." [Tafsir al-Tabari 25/68.] Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in this same form from his father, from Ibn Umar, from Sufyan, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn Abbas, as mentioned. [Variant: "Ibn Jarir narrated it in this form, from Ibn Abi Hatim, from his father..."] This chain is sound (sahih) up to Ibn Abbas, the scholar of the Ummah (habr al-ummah) and the interpreter of the Qur'an (turjuman al-Qur'an). This is also the view of all those among the Companions and Successors who agreed with him, together with the raised (marfu') hadiths from the sound and fair (hisan) collections and others, which we have cited, and which provide sufficient proof and clear indication that the smoke is one of the awaited signs, while it is also the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky brings a clear smoke﴾, that is, clear and evident, which everyone sees. As for what Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, explained: it is only an imagining they saw in their eyes from the intensity of hunger and hardship. Similarly His saying: ﴿covering the people﴾, that is, it envelops them and overwhelms them; and if it were an imagined matter specific to the polytheists of Makkah, it would not have been said: ﴿covering the people﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿This is a painful punishment﴾, that is, it will be said to them as a rebuke and reproach, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The Day they will be pushed into the Fire of Hell with a violent push: "This is the Fire which you used to deny."﴾ [al-Tur 52:13–14], or some of them will say it to others.

* *

Their saying: "Our Lord, remove the punishment from us; indeed we are believers" (Qur'an 44:12). That is, the disbelievers, when they witness Allah's punishment and retribution, will say, seeking its lifting and removal from them, like His saying: "If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire, and they say, 'Would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers'" (Qur'an 6:27). Likewise His saying: "And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, 'Our Lord, delay us for a brief term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.' Did you not previously swear that for you there would be no decline?" (Qur'an 14:44). And so He says here: "How will they have the reminder, when there has come to them a clear messenger, and then they turned away from him and said, 'A taught one, a madman'" (Qur'an 44:13–14).

He says: How can they have remembrance, when We have sent to them a messenger clear in the message and the warning, and yet they turned away from him and did not agree with him, but rather denied him and said, "A taught one, a madman." This is like His saying, exalted is He: "On that Day man will remember, but how will the remembrance benefit him? He will say, 'Oh, would that I had sent ahead for my life'" (Qur'an 89:23–24). And His saying, exalted is He: "If only you could see when they are terrified and there is no escape, and they are seized from a near place. And they say, 'We believe in Him.' But how can they reach [faith] from a distant place? And they had disbelieved in it before, and they hurl [accusations] about the unseen from a distant place. And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as was done with their counterparts before; indeed they were in disquieting doubt" (Qur'an 34:51–54).

* *

His saying: "Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little; indeed you will return" (Qur'an 44:15) admits of two meanings:

The first: that Allah says, "Even if We removed the punishment from you and returned you to the worldly abode, you would return to what you were in of disbelief and denial," like His saying: "Even if We had mercy upon them and removed what harm is upon them, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly" (Qur'an 23:75), and like His saying: "And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars" (Qur'an 6:28).

The second: that the intended meaning is: "We will delay the punishment from you a little after its causes have been established and it has reached you, while you remain persisting in what you are in of rebellion and misguidance." Removing it from them does not necessarily mean that it has touched them, like His saying, exalted is He: "Except the people of Yunus; when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and We gave them enjoyment for a time" (Qur'an 10:98). The punishment had not touched them and reached them, but its cause had been established upon them. Nor does it necessarily follow that they had ceased from their disbelief and then returned to it. Allah, exalted is He, related about Shu'ayb that he said to his people when they said: "We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you, from our town, or you will return to our religion." He said: "Even if we were unwilling? We would have fabricated a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion after Allah has delivered us from it" (Qur'an 7:88–89). Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, had never been upon their religion and way.

Qatadah said: "Indeed you will return" means to the punishment of Allah.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: "The Day We will seize with the greatest seizing; indeed We will take retribution" (Qur'an 44:16). Ibn Mas'ud interpreted that as the Day of Badr. This is the view of a group who agreed with Ibn Mas'ud's interpretation of the smoke as explained earlier. It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas [and a group] through the narration of al-'Awfi from him, and from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and a group, and it is possible.

The apparent meaning is that it is the Day of Resurrection, although the Day of Badr was also a day of seizing.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub related to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, Khalid al-Hadhdha' related to us, from 'Ikrimah who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "The greatest seizing is the Day of Badr," and I say: it is the Day of Resurrection.

This is a sound chain from him, and al-Hasan al-Basri and 'Ikrimah in the more correct of the two reports from him, hold this view.

Allah the Exalted says: And We certainly tested before these polytheists the people of Pharaoh, who were the Copts of Egypt. ﴿And there came to them a noble messenger﴾, meaning Musa (Moses), his interlocutor, upon him be peace, saying: ﴿Deliver to me the servants of Allah﴾, like His saying: ﴿So send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord, and peace will be upon whoever follows guidance﴾ [Ta-Ha: 47].
* *
And His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾, meaning: one entrusted with what I convey to you.
* *
And His saying: ﴿And do not exalt yourselves over Allah﴾, meaning: do not be arrogant toward following His signs, and toward submitting to His proofs and believing in His evidences, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation﴾ [Ghafir: 60].
﴿Indeed, I bring you clear authority﴾, meaning: a manifest and evident proof, which is the signs and conclusive evidences that Allah sent him with.
﴿And indeed, I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from your stoning me﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Salih said: it is stoning with the tongue, which is insult. Qatadah said: it is stoning with stones.
Meaning: I seek refuge in Allah, who created me and you, from your reaching me with harm, whether by word or deed.
﴿And if you do not believe me, then leave me alone﴾, meaning: do not confront me, and leave the matter between me and you in peaceful terms until Allah judges between us. So when his stay among them was prolonged, and he established the proofs of Allah against them, and all of that only increased them in disbelief and obstinacy, he invoked his Lord against them with a supplication that took effect upon them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Musa said, "Our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world. Our Lord, that they may lead astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so they will not believe until they see the painful punishment." He said, "Your supplication has been answered, so remain steadfast"﴾ [Yunus: 88–89]. And thus He said here: ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "These are a criminal people"﴾. At that point Allah the Exalted commanded him to take the Children of Israel out from among them, without the order or consultation or permission of Pharaoh. For this reason He said: ﴿So depart with My servants by night; indeed, you will be pursued﴾, as He said: ﴿And We revealed to Musa, "Travel with My servants by night and strike for them a dry path through the sea; you will not fear being overtaken, nor will you be afraid"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 77].
* *
And His saying here: ﴿And leave the sea parted; indeed, they are an army to be drowned﴾. That was because Musa, upon him be peace, when he and the Children of Israel had crossed the sea, wanted to strike it with his staff so that it would return as it was, to become a barrier between them and Pharaoh, so that he could not reach them. So Allah commanded him to leave it in its state, still, and gave him good news that they were an army that would be drowned in it, and that he would not fear being overtaken and would not be afraid.
Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾ as it is, and proceed. Mujahid said: ﴿Parted﴾ means a dry path as it is; he says: do not order him to return; leave it until the last of them has passed. Likewise said 'Ikrimah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, Ka'b al-Ahbar, Simak ibn Harb, and others.
Then He the Exalted said: ﴿How many gardens they left behind﴾, which are the orchards, ﴿and springs and crops﴾, by which is meant the rivers and wells, ﴿and noble dwellings﴾, which are the noble, pleasant residences and the good places.
Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿Noble dwellings﴾ means the pulpits.
Ibn Lahi'ah narrated from Wahb ibn 'Abd Allah al-Mu'afiri, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Nile of Egypt is the chief of rivers; Allah subjected to it every river between the east and the west and made them submissive to it. When Allah wishes to cause the Nile of Egypt to flow, He commands every river to supply it, so the rivers supply it with their water, and Allah causes springs to gush forth from the earth for it. When its flow reaches what Allah wills, Allah reveals to every water to return to its source.
And regarding His saying: ﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind, and crops and noble dwellings, and luxury they were in, enjoying﴾, he said: The gardens were on both banks of this Nile, from its beginning to its end, on both sides together, from Aswan to Rashid. It had nine channels: the channel of Alexandria, the channel of Damietta, the channel of Sardus, the channel of Memphis, the channel of al-Fayyum, and the channel of al-Manha, connected, with nothing of them cut off from another. And crops were between the two mountains, all of it from the beginning of Egypt to the furthest point the water reaches. All the land of Egypt was irrigated from sixteen cubits, because of what they measured and arranged regarding its bridges, dams, and channels.
﴿And luxury they were in, enjoying﴾, meaning: a life in which they would take pleasure, eating what they wished and wearing what they loved, along with wealth, status, and rule over the lands. All of that was stripped from them in a single morning. They departed from the world and went to Hell, and wretched is the destination. The Children of Israel took over the Egyptian lands and those Pharaonic storehouses and Coptic kingdoms, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Thus, and We bequeathed them to the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 59]. He said in another place: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed. And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of what they endured, and We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had constructed and what they had built﴾ [al-A'raf: 137]. And here He said: ﴿Thus, and We bequeathed them to another people﴾, who were the Children of Israel, as has preceded.
* *
And His saying: ﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep for them﴾, meaning: they had no righteous deeds ascending through the gates of heaven so that it would weep over their loss, nor did they have on earth places where they worshipped Allah so that it would miss them. Therefore they deserved not to be given respite or delay, because of their disbelief, their crimes, their insolence, and their obstinacy.

Then He the Exalted said: ﴿How many gardens they left behind﴾, which are the orchards, ﴿and springs and crops﴾, by which is meant the rivers and wells, ﴿and noble dwellings﴾, which are the noble, pleasant residences and the good places.
Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿Noble dwellings﴾ means the pulpits.

When Allah wishes to cause the Nile of Egypt to flow, He commands every river to supply it, so the rivers supply it with their water, and Allah causes springs to gush forth from the earth for it. When its flow reaches what Allah wills, Allah reveals to every water to return to its source.

It had nine channels: the channel of Alexandria, the channel of Damietta, the channel of Sardus, the channel of Memphis, the channel of al-Fayyum, and the channel of al-Manha, connected, with nothing of them cut off from another. And crops were between the two mountains, all of it from the beginning of Egypt to the furthest point the water reaches. All the land of Egypt was irrigated from sixteen cubits, because of what they measured and arranged regarding its bridges, dams, and channels.

And here He said: ﴿Thus, and We bequeathed them to another people﴾, who were the Children of Israel, as has preceded.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾, meaning: one entrusted with what I convey to you.
* *
And His saying: ﴿And do not exalt yourselves over Allah﴾, meaning: do not be arrogant toward following His signs, and toward submitting to His proofs and believing in His evidences, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation﴾ [Ghafir: 60].

Al-'Awfi narrated similarly from Ibn 'Abbas.

Uthman ibn Affan was killed while besieged and wronged, and none of that occurred. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was killed in the prayer niche during the dawn prayer, and it was as though the Muslims had not been struck by any calamity before that, yet none of that occurred. And this is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who is the master of mankind in this world and the Hereafter; on the day he died, none of what they mentioned occurred. And on the day Ibrahim, son of the Prophet (ﷺ), died, the sun eclipsed, and the people said: "The sun eclipsed for the death of Ibrahim." So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, led them in the eclipse prayer, delivered a sermon to them, and made clear that the sun and the moon do not eclipse for the death of anyone or for his life. (Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 1043, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 915.)

* *

* *

All the land of Egypt was irrigated from sixteen cubits, because of what they measured and arranged regarding its bridges, dams, and channels.

And here He said: ﴿Thus, and We bequeathed them to another people﴾, who were the Children of Israel, as has preceded.
* *
And His saying: ﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep for them﴾, meaning: they had no righteous deeds ascending through the gates of heaven so that it would weep over their loss, nor did they have on earth places where they worshipped Allah so that it would miss them. The Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Basri narrated to us, Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaydah narrated to us, Yazid al-Raqashi narrated to me, Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "There is no servant but that he has two doors in heaven: a door from which his provision descends, and a door into which his deed and his speech enter. When he dies, they both miss him and weep over him." And he recited this verse: ﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep for them﴾. It is mentioned that they had not done any righteous deed on earth for which they would be wept over, and no good speech or righteous deed of theirs ascended to heaven so that it would miss them and weep over them. [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/160). It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (3255), via Musa ibn 'Ubaydah with the same wording in abridged form, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it to be marfu' except through this chain, and Musa ibn 'Ubaydah and Yazid ibn Aban al-Raqashi are weak in hadith."]
Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, who was al-Rabadhi.
Ibn Jarir said: Yahya ibn Talhah narrated to me, 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to me, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd al-Hadrami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Islam began strange and will return strange. He said to him: "You have asked me about something no one has asked me before. There is no servant except that he has a place of prayer on earth, and an ascent for his deed from heaven. The family of Pharaoh had no righteous deed on earth, nor any deed ascending to heaven." Then 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, recited: ﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep for them, nor were they given respite﴾.
Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Talq ibn Ghannam narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Mansur, from Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "O Abu 'Abbas, what do you say about the saying of Allah: ﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep for them, nor were they given respite﴾? Do the heaven and earth weep over anyone?" He said: "Yes. There is no creature but that it has a door in heaven from which its provision descends and through which its deed ascends. When a believer dies, the door of heaven through which his deed used to ascend and his provision used to descend is closed, and it weeps over him; and when his place of prayer on earth, where he used to pray and mention Allah, is missed, it weeps over him. But the people of Pharaoh had no good traces on earth, and no good ever ascended to Allah from them, so the heaven and earth did not weep over them." [Tafsir al-Tabari (25/74).]
Al-'Awfi narrated similarly from Ibn 'Abbas.
Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Yahya al-Qattat, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: It used to be said: the earth weeps for the believer for forty mornings. Likewise said Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and others.
Mujahid also said: No believer dies but that the heaven and earth weep over him for forty mornings. He said: I said to him: "Does the earth weep?" He said: "Are you surprised? Why would the earth not weep over a servant who used to make it flourish with bowing and prostration? And why would the heaven not weep over a servant whose takbir and tasbih in it made a sound like the buzzing of bees?"
Qatadah said: They were too insignificant in the sight of Allah for the heaven and earth to weep over them.
Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abd al-Salam ibn 'Asim narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us, al-Mustawrid ibn Sabiq narrated to us, from 'Ubayd al-Muktib, from Ibrahim, who said: Since the world existed, the heaven has wept only over two. I said to 'Ubayd: "Do not the heaven and earth weep over the believer?" He said: "That is their station, where his deed ascends." He said: "Do you know what the weeping of the heaven is?" I said: "No." He said: "It turns red and becomes like rose, like oil. When Yahya ibn Zakariyya was killed, the heaven turned red and dripped blood. And when Husayn ibn 'Ali was killed, the heaven turned red."

Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn Amr (Zunayj) narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, who said: When Husayn ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, was killed, the horizons of the sky turned red for four months. Yazid said: "Its reddening was its weeping." And thus said al-Suddi al-Kabir.

Ata al-Khurasani said: "Its weeping: that its edges turned red."

They also mentioned, regarding the killing of Husayn, that on that day no stone was turned over except that fresh blood was found beneath it, that the sun eclipsed, the horizon turned red, and stones fell. Then He the Exalted said: ﴿How many gardens they left behind﴾, which are the orchards, ﴿and springs and crops﴾, by which is meant the rivers and wells, ﴿and noble dwellings﴾, which are the noble, pleasant residences and the good places.
Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿Noble dwellings﴾ means the pulpits.

When Allah wishes to cause the Nile of Egypt to flow, He commands every river to supply it, so the rivers supply it with their water, and Allah causes springs to gush forth from the earth for it. When its flow reaches what Allah wills, Allah reveals to every water to return to its source.

It had nine channels: the channel of Alexandria, the channel of Damietta, the channel of Sardus, the channel of Memphis, the channel of al-Fayyum, and the channel of al-Manha, connected, with nothing of them cut off from another. And crops were between the two mountains, all of it from the beginning of Egypt to the furthest point the water reaches. All the land of Egypt was irrigated from sixteen cubits, because of what they measured and arranged regarding its bridges, dams, and channels.

And here He said: ﴿Thus, and We bequeathed them to another people﴾, who were the Children of Israel, as has preceded.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾, meaning: one entrusted with what I convey to you.
* *
And His saying: ﴿And do not exalt yourselves over Allah﴾, meaning: do not be arrogant toward following His signs, and toward submitting to His proofs and believing in His evidences, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation﴾ [Ghafir: 60].

Al-'Awfi narrated similarly from Ibn 'Abbas.

Uthman ibn Affan was killed while besieged and wronged, and none of that occurred. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was killed in the prayer niche during the dawn prayer, and it was as though the Muslims had not been struck by any calamity before that, yet none of that occurred. And this is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who is the master of mankind in this world and the Hereafter; on the day he died, none of what they mentioned occurred. And on the day Ibrahim, son of the Prophet (ﷺ), died, the sun eclipsed, and the people said: "The sun eclipsed for the death of Ibrahim." So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, led them in the eclipse prayer, delivered a sermon to them, and made clear that the sun and the moon do not eclipse for the death of anyone or for his life. (Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 1043, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 915.)

* *

* *

All the land of Egypt was irrigated from sixteen cubits, because of what they measured and arranged regarding its bridges, dams, and channels.

And here He said: ﴿Thus, and We bequeathed them to another people﴾, who were the Children of Israel, as has preceded.
* *
And His saying: ﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep for them﴾, meaning: they had no righteous deeds ascending through the gates of heaven so that it would weep over their loss, nor did they have on earth places where they worshipped Allah so that it would miss them. The Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Basri narrated to us, Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaydah narrated to us, Yazid al-Raqashi narrated to me, Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "There is no servant but that he has two doors in heaven: a door from which his provision descends, and a door into which his deed and his speech enter. When he dies, they both miss him and weep over him." And he recited this verse: ﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep for them﴾. It is mentioned that they had not done any righteous deed on earth for which they would be wept over, and no good speech or righteous deed of theirs ascended to heaven so that it would miss them and weep over them. [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/160). It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (3255), via Musa ibn 'Ubaydah with the same wording in abridged form, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it to be marfu' except through this chain, and Musa ibn 'Ubaydah and Yazid ibn Aban al-Raqashi are weak in hadith."]
Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, who was al-Rabadhi.
Ibn Jarir said: Yahya ibn Talhah narrated to me, 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to me, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd al-Hadrami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Islam began strange and will return strange. He said to him: "You have asked me about something no one has asked me before. There is no servant except that he has a place of prayer on earth, and an ascent for his deed from heaven. The family of Pharaoh had no righteous deed on earth, nor any deed ascending to heaven." Then 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, recited: ﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep for them, nor were they given respite﴾.
Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Talq ibn Ghannam narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Mansur, from Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "O Abu 'Abbas, what do you say about the saying of Allah: ﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep for them, nor were they given respite﴾? Do the heaven and earth weep over anyone?" He said: "Yes. There is no creature but that it has a door in heaven from which its provision descends and through which its deed ascends. When a believer dies, the door of heaven through which his deed used to ascend and his provision used to descend is closed, and it weeps over him; and when his place of prayer on earth, where he used to pray and mention Allah, is missed, it weeps over him. But the people of Pharaoh had no good traces on earth, and no good ever ascended to Allah from them, so the heaven and earth did not weep over them." [Tafsir al-Tabari (25/74).]
Al-'Awfi narrated similarly from Ibn 'Abbas.
Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Yahya al-Qattat, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: It used to be said: the earth weeps for the believer for forty mornings. Likewise said Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and others.
Mujahid also said: No believer dies but that the heaven and earth weep over him for forty mornings. He said: I said to him: "Does the earth weep?" He said: "Are you surprised? Why would the earth not weep over a servant who used to make it flourish with bowing and prostration? And why would the heaven not weep over a servant whose takbir and tasbih in it made a sound like the buzzing of bees?"
Qatadah said: They were too insignificant in the sight of Allah for the heaven and earth to weep over them.
Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abd al-Salam ibn 'Asim narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us, al-Mustawrid ibn Sabiq narrated to us, from 'Ubayd al-Muktib, from Ibrahim, who said: Since the world existed, the heaven has wept only over two. I said to 'Ubayd: "Do not the heaven and earth weep over the believer?" He said: "That is their station, where his deed ascends." He said: "Do you know what the weeping of the heaven is?" I said: "No." He said: "It turns red and becomes like rose, like oil. When Yahya ibn Zakariyya was killed, the heaven turned red and dripped blood. And when Husayn ibn 'Ali was killed, the heaven turned red."

Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn Amr (Zunayj) narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, who said: When Husayn ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, was killed, the horizons of the sky turned red for four months. Yazid said: "Its reddening was its weeping." And thus said al-Suddi al-Kabir.

Ata al-Khurasani said: "Its weeping: that its edges turned red."

They also mentioned, regarding the killing of Husayn, that on that day no stone was turned over except that fresh blood was found beneath it, that the sun eclipsed, the horizon turned red, and stones fell. When a believer dies, the door of heaven through which his deed used to ascend and his provision used to descend is closed, and it weeps over him; and when his place of prayer on earth, where he used to pray and mention Allah, is missed, it weeps over him. But the people of Pharaoh had no good traces on earth, and no good ever ascended to Allah from them, so the heaven and earth did not weep over them." [Tafsir al-Tabari (25/74).]
Al-'Awfi narrated similarly from Ibn 'Abbas.
Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Yahya al-Qattat, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: It used to be said: the earth weeps for the believer for forty mornings. Likewise said Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and others.
Mujahid also said: No believer dies but that the heaven and earth weep over him for forty mornings. He said: I said to him: "Does the earth weep?" He said: "Are you surprised? Why would the earth not weep over a servant who used to make it flourish with bowing and prostration? And why would the heaven not weep over a servant whose takbir and tasbih in it made a sound like the buzzing of bees?"
Qatadah said: They were too insignificant in the sight of Allah for the heaven and earth to weep over them.
Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abd al-Salam ibn 'Asim narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us, al-Mustawrid ibn Sabiq narrated to us, from 'Ubayd al-Muktib, from Ibrahim, who said: Since the world existed, the heaven has wept only over two. I said to 'Ubayd: "Do not the heaven and earth weep over the believer?" He said: "That is their station, where his deed ascends." He said: "Do you know what the weeping of the heaven is?" I said: "No." He said: "It turns red and becomes like rose, like oil. When Yahya ibn Zakariyya was killed, the heaven turned red and dripped blood. And when Husayn ibn 'Ali was killed, the heaven turned red."

Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn Amr (Zunayj) narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, who said: When Husayn ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, was killed, the horizons of the sky turned red for four months. Yazid said: "Its reddening was its weeping." And thus said al-Suddi al-Kabir.

Ata al-Khurasani said: "Its weeping: that its edges turned red."

They also mentioned, regarding the killing of Husayn, that on that day no stone was turned over except that fresh blood was found beneath it, that the sun eclipsed, the horizon turned red, and stones fell. But there is scrutiny regarding all of this, and the apparent position is that it is from the foolishness and lies of the Shi'ah, in order to magnify the matter, and there is no doubt that the matter is great. But what they invented and lied about did not happen. What is greater than that did happen: the killing of Husayn, may Allah be pleased with him, and none of what they mentioned occurred. His father, Ali ibn Abi Talib, was killed, and he is by consensus more excellent than him, and none of that occurred for him. Uthman ibn Affan was killed while besieged and wronged, and none of that occurred. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was killed in the prayer niche during the dawn prayer, and it was as though the Muslims had not been struck by any calamity before that, yet none of that occurred. And this is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who is the master of mankind in this world and the Hereafter; on the day he died, none of what they mentioned occurred. And on the day Ibrahim, son of the Prophet (ﷺ), died, the sun eclipsed, and the people said: "The sun eclipsed for the death of Ibrahim." So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, led them in the eclipse prayer, delivered a sermon to them, and made clear that the sun and the moon do not eclipse for the death of anyone or for his life. (Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 1043, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 915.)

* *

His saying: ﴿And We certainly delivered the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment, from Pharaoh. Indeed, he was haughty among the transgressors.﴾ He, exalted is He, bestows favour upon them by this, since He rescued them from what they were in of humiliation and degradation by Pharaoh, and his subjecting them to degrading and arduous labours.

* *

His saying: ﴿from Pharaoh. Indeed, he was haughty [among the transgressors]﴾ meaning: arrogant, tyrannical, obstinate, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions﴾ [al-Qasas: 4].

* *

His saying: ﴿So they were arrogant, and they were a haughty people﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 46], and His saying: ﴿So they were arrogant in the land, and they were not those who could escape﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 39]. Pharaoh was excessive in his affair, foolish in his opinion regarding himself.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We certainly chose them with knowledge over the worlds﴾. Mujahid said: ﴿We chose them with knowledge over the worlds﴾ means over those who were among them in their time. Qatadah said: They were chosen over the people of their era. It was said: "Indeed, every era has a world (a people of that age)." This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "O Musa, I have chosen you over the people"﴾ [al-A'raf: 144], meaning the people of his time, and like His saying to Maryam: ﴿and chose you over the women of the worlds﴾ [Al 'Imran: 42], meaning in her time; for Khadijah is better than her, and likewise Asiyah bint Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh, is either better than her or equal to her in virtue, and the virtue of Aishah over women is like the virtue of thareed over the rest of food.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We gave them of the signs﴾, meaning proofs, evidences and supernatural occurrences, ﴿in which was a clear trial﴾, meaning a manifest, evident test for whoever was guided by it.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 44, verses 34–37:

He, the Exalted, says, rebuking the polytheists for their denial of the Resurrection and the Return, and [denying] that there is anything beyond this worldly life, that there is no life after death, and no resurrection or rising. They argue by [citing] their forefathers who passed away and did not return. [They say:] ﴿Then bring back our fathers, if you are truthful.﴾ This is a false argument and a corrupt doubt, for the Return (al-ma'ad) is only on the Day of Resurrection, not in this abode, [but] [[addition from MS T and MS A.]] after its completion, its passing away, and its ending. Then God will bring the worlds back into a new creation, and He will make the wrongdoers fuel for the Fire of Hell, on a day when you [[in MS T: "you" (plural); in MS M: "you"]] will be witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger will be a witness over you.

Then He, the Exalted, says, threatening them and warning them of His might, which cannot be repelled, as it befell their likes and counterparts among the polytheists and deniers of the Resurrection, and the people of Tubba' — and they are Saba' — when God destroyed them, ruined their lands, scattered them through the lands, and dispersed them utterly, as has already been mentioned in Surah Saba'. That surah opens with the denial of the Resurrection by the polytheists, and likewise here He compares them to those. They were Arabs from Qahtan, just as these [Quraysh] are Arabs from 'Adnan. Himyar, who are Saba', used to name any man who ruled among them Tubba', just as Kisra is said of whoever ruled the Persians, Qaysar of whoever ruled the Romans, Pharaoh of whoever ruled Egypt as a disbeliever, and al-Najashi of whoever ruled Abyssinia, and other such generic titles. It happened that one of their Tubba' set out from Yemen and traveled through the lands until he reached Samarqand. His rule grew strong, his authority and army became great, his kingdom and lands expanded, and his subjects multiplied. It was he who founded al-Hirah. It happened that he passed by the Prophet's city [Madinah] in the days of ignorance (jahiliyyah). He wanted to fight its people, but they defended themselves and fought him by day, while by night they hosted him. He felt ashamed before them and refrained from them. He took with him two rabbis from the rabbis of the Jews who had advised him and informed him that he had no path to this town, for it is the emigration place (muhajar) of a prophet who will appear at the end of time. He turned back from it and took the two with him to the land of Yemen. When he passed by Makkah, he wanted to demolish the Ka'bah, but the two rabbis forbade him from that as well, and informed him of the greatness of this House, that it was built by Ibrahim the Friend [of God], and that a great affair would come to it through the hands of that prophet who would be sent at the end of time. So he honored it, circumambulated it, and covered it with robes (mula'), wrappings (wasa'il), and silk (habir). Then he returned to Yemen and called its people to Judaism along with him. At that time the religion of Musa, peace be upon him, was present there, with those who were upon guidance before the mission of the Messiah, peace be upon him. So most of the people of Yemen became Jews along with him. The Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq has related the full story in his book *al-Sirah* [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/19).]], and the Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir has written an extensive biography of him in his *Tarikh*, including many things we have mentioned and many we have not [[Tarikh Dimashq (3/500, manuscript section).]]. He mentioned that he ruled Damascus, and that when he reviewed his horses, they were lined up for him from Damascus to Yemen. Then he related, by way of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b [[In MSS T and A: "Dhu'ayb".]], from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "I do not know whether the hudud (prescribed punishments) are an expiation for those who receive them or not; I do not know whether Tubba' was a cursed man [[In MS T: "trustworthy".]] or not; and I do not know whether Dhu al-Qarnayn was a prophet or a king." Another [narrator] said: "Was 'Uzayr a prophet or not?" Likewise, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Zahrani [[In MS M: "al-Tabarani".]], from 'Abd al-Razzaq [[Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (1/36) by way of 'Abd al-Razzaq, and Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan, no. 4674, by way of 'Abd al-Razzaq, except that he said "'Aziz" instead of "Dhu al-Qarnayn."]].

Al-Daraqutni said: 'Abd al-Razzaq alone transmitted it [[The Hafiz Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said in *Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm wa Fadlih* (2/50): "The hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, 'Indeed the hudud are an expiation for those who receive them,' is more authentic and more firmly established in its chain," and then he quoted it by way of al-Bukhari with its chain to 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]]. Then Ibn 'Asakir narrated by way of Muhammad ibn Kurayb, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, as a marfu' report: "'Uzayr — I do not know whether he was a prophet or not; and I do not know whether Tubba' was cursed or not." [[Tarikh Dimashq (3/501, manuscript section).]]

Then he mentioned what has come concerning the prohibition of insulting him and cursing him, as will come. It seems — and God knows best — that he was a disbeliever who then embraced Islam and followed the religion of the Speaker [with God] (al-Kalim) [[In MSS T, M, and A: "al-Khalil" (the Friend)]] through the hands of the rabbis of the Jews in that time, [who were] upon the truth before the mission of the Messiah, peace be upon him. He performed Hajj to the House in the time of the Jurhumites, covered it with robes and wrappings of silk and hibar, sacrificed six thousand camels there, and magnified and honored it. Then he returned to Yemen. Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir related his story in full through many lengthy and detailed chains, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, and Ka'b al-Ahbar. The final reference for all of that is to 'Abd Allah ibn Salam as well, and he is the most firmly established, the most senior, and the most knowledgeable. Likewise, Wahb ibn Munabbih and Muhammad ibn Ishaq in the *Sirah* related his story, as is well known therein. Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir was confused in some of the narrations, mixing the biography of this Tubba' with that of another who came long after him by a great span of time. This Tubba' mentioned in the Qur'an had his people embrace Islam through his hands, but after he died they returned to worshipping idols and fire, so God punished them, as He mentioned in Surah Saba'. We have expounded their story there, and to God belongs all praise and grace.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Tubba' covered the Ka'bah, and Sa'id used to forbid insulting him.

This Tubba' is Tubba' al-Awsat (the middle Tubba'), and his name is As'ad Abu Karib ibn Malikikarib [[In MS M: "Malikarib."]] al-Yamani. They mention that he ruled over his people for three hundred and twenty-six years, and there was none among Himyar who reigned longer than he, and he died about seven hundred years before the mission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They mention that when the two rabbis of the Jews of Madinah told him that this town was the emigration place of another prophet at the end of time, whose name is Ahmad, he composed poetry about that and entrusted it to the people of Madinah. They used to inherit it and narrate it from generation to generation. Among those who memorized it was Abu Ayyub Khalid ibn Zayd, in whose house the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed. The poem is:

"I bear witness concerning Ahmad that he
is a Messenger from Allah, Creator of the souls..."

"If my life were extended to his life,
I would be his minister and his cousin..."

"And I would fight his enemies with the sword,
and relieve his chest of every grief..."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned that a grave was dug in Sana' in Islamic times, and in it they found two women intact, and at their heads was a silver plate on which was written in gold: "This is the grave of Hubba and Lamis" — and it is narrated: "Hubba and Tumadir" — "the two daughters of Tubba', who died. They both bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and they associate nothing with Him. Upon this the righteous died before them."

We have mentioned in "Surah Saba'" the poetry of Saba' on this matter too.

Qatadah said: It was related to us that Ka'b used to say concerning Tubba': "He was described in the manner of a righteous man; God censured his people but did not censure him." He said: 'A'ishah used to say: "Do not curse Tubba', for he was indeed a righteous man."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Safwan narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Abu Zur'ah — meaning 'Amr ibn Jabir al-Hadrami — who said: I heard Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not curse Tubba', for he had indeed embraced Islam."

Imam Ahmad narrated it in his *Musnad* by way of al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibn Lahi'ah, with the same [text] [[al-Musnad (5/340). Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in *Takhrij al-Kashshaf*: "In its chain is Ibn Lahi'ah and 'Amr ibn Jabir, and both are weak."]].

Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Abbar narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bazzah narrated to us, Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Do not curse Tubba', for he had embraced Islam" [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/296). Al-Haythami said in *al-Majma'* (8/769): "In it is Ahmad ibn Abi Bazzah al-Makki, whom I do not know, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]].

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I do not know whether Tubba' was a prophet or not a prophet" [[Also narrated by al-Tha'labi in his *Tafsir*, as in *Takhrij al-Kashshaf* of al-Zaylai (3/270), by way of 'Abd al-Razzaq with this wording.]].

It has already come with this chain from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, as Ibn 'Asakir quoted it: "I do not know whether Tubba' was cursed or not." And God knows best.

Ibn 'Asakir also narrated it by way of Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Badi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, as a mawquf (ending with a companion) report.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: 'Imran Abu al-Hudhayl narrated to us, Tamim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me, who said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "Do not curse Tubba', for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden [[In MSS T and A: "had forbidden."]] cursing him" [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/171).]].
