Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 44, verses 38–42:

He, exalted is He, says, informing about His justice and His transcendence above play, idle sport, and falsehood, as in His saying: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾ [Sad: 27], and His saying ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose, and that you would not be returned to Us? So exalted is Allah, the True King; there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115, 116].

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgement is the appointed time for them all﴾. It is the Day of Resurrection, on which Allah will separate between the creatures, punishing the disbelievers and rewarding the believers.

* *

His saying ﴿the appointed time for them all﴾ means: He will gather them all, the first of them and the last of them.

﴿The Day when no protector will avail a protector at all﴾, meaning: no relative will benefit a relative. This is like His saying: ﴿And when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask about one another﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 101], and like His saying ﴿and no intimate friend will ask after an intimate friend, though they will be shown to one another﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 10, 11], meaning: no friend will ask his brother about his condition while he sees him plainly.

* *

His saying ﴿nor will they be helped﴾ means: no relative will help his relative, nor will help come to him from outside.

Then He said: ﴿except those on whom Allah has mercy﴾, meaning: on that Day, none will benefit except those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has shown mercy to among His creation [[In A: "except the mercy of Allah toward His creation".]] ﴿Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful﴾, meaning: He is Mighty, possessor of vast mercy.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 44, verse 51–59:

When Allah (may He be exalted) mentioned the state of the wretched, He followed it with mention of the state of the blessed (and for this reason the Qur'an is called "al-mathani" [the oft-repeated]). So He said: ﴿Indeed, the righteous [al-muttaqin]﴾, meaning: those who were mindful of Allah in this world, ﴿will be in a secure place﴾, meaning: in the Hereafter, which is Paradise, where they will be safe from death and expulsion, from every worry, sorrow, distress, weariness and fatigue, from Satan and his plotting, and from all other calamities and afflictions.

﴿Among gardens and springs﴾. This is in contrast to what those (the wretched) will have of the tree of zaqqum and the drinking of boiling water.

* *

His saying (exalted is He): ﴿They will wear of fine silk and brocade﴾. Sundus is fine silk, like shirts and the like. ﴿Istabraq﴾ is that which has a sheen and gleam, such as the rich garments and what is worn over the finest fabrics. ﴿Facing one another﴾, meaning: on couches, none of them sitting with his back to another.

* *

His saying: ﴿Thus, and We will pair them with large-eyed houris﴾, meaning: this bounty, along with what We have granted them of wives, the beautiful large-eyed houris, ﴿whom no man or jinn has touched before them﴾ [al-Rahman: 56, 74], ﴿as if they were rubies and coral﴾ [al-Rahman: 58], ﴿Is the reward for good anything but good?﴾ [al-Rahman: 60].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Nuh ibn Habib narrated to us, Nasr ibn Muzahim al-Attar narrated to us, Umar ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from a man, from Anas, (whose narration Nuh raised to the Prophet ﷺ), who said: "If a houri were to spit into a deep sea, that water would become sweet from the sweetness of her saliva." [Abu Nu'aym narrated it in Sifat al-Jannah, no. 386, by another route: from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Hasani, from Mansur al-Wasiti, from Abu al-Nadr al-Abbar, from Anas, raised to the Prophet, with similar wording.]

* *

His saying: ﴿Therein they will call for every kind of fruit, secure﴾, meaning: whatever kinds of fruit they request will be brought to them, and they will be secure that it will not be cut off or withheld, but rather it will come to them whenever they wish.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will not taste death therein, except the first death﴾. This is an exception that emphasizes the negation; it is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), and its meaning is that they will never taste death therein. As is established in the two Sahihs, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Death will be brought in the form of a white-black ram, and it will be stopped between Paradise and Hell, and then it will be slaughtered. Then it will be said: O people of Paradise, eternity, with no death; and O people of Hell, eternity, with no death." The hadith has already been mentioned in the commentary on Surah Maryam [see the takhrij of the hadith at verse 39 of Surah Maryam].

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Muslim al-Agharr, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It will be said to the people of Paradise: Indeed, for you is health, so you will never fall ill; indeed, for you is life, so you will never die; indeed, for you is bounty, so you will never be miserable; indeed, for you is youth, so you will never grow old." Muslim narrated it from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh and Abd ibn Humayd, both from Abd al-Razzaq with the same chain. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2837.]

Thus Abu Ishaq and the people of Iraq say "Abu Muslim al-Agharr," while the people of Medina say "Abu Abd Allah al-Agharr." [The first is the correct one, as Imam al-Mizzi explained in Tahdhib al-Kamal.]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud al-Sijistani said: Ahmad ibn Hafs narrated to us, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from al-Hajjaj — that is, Ibn Hajjaj — from Ubada [in some copies: Qatada], from Ubayd Allah ibn Amr, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever is mindful of Allah enters Paradise, where he will enjoy bounty and will not be miserable, and will live therein and will not die; his garments will not wear out, and his youth will not fade." [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 4895 (Majma' al-Bahrayn), by way of Ahmad ibn Hafs.]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Ubayd Allah al-Raqqi narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Imran ibn al-Rabi' al-Kufi narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ was asked: "Do the people of Paradise sleep?" He said: "Sleep is the brother of death, and the people of Paradise do not sleep." [Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 4875 (Majma' al-Bahrayn); in its chain is Mus'ab ibn Ibrahim al-Absi, who is munkar al-hadith.]

Likewise, Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Sadaqa al-Misri narrated to us, al-Miqdam ibn Dawud narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Sleep is the brother of death, and the people of Paradise do not sleep." [Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilya (7/90), by way of Ahmad ibn al-Qasim from al-Miqdam ibn Dawud, and said: "Gharib from the hadith of al-Thawri; it was narrated solely by Abd Allah."]

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: al-Fadl ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, do the people of Paradise sleep?" He said: "No, sleep is the brother of death." Then he said: "We do not know anyone who transmitted this from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, except al-Thawri, nor from al-Thawri except al-Firyabi." [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3517 (Kashf al-Astar); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/415): "The narrators of al-Bazzar are the narrators of the Sahih."] Thus he said, though the contrary has already been mentioned, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And He protected them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾, meaning: alongside this great, enduring bounty, He has protected them, kept them safe, saved them and distanced them from the painful punishment in the levels of Hell. Thus they have attained what they sought and were delivered from what they feared. For this reason He said: ﴿As a bounty from your Lord. That is the great triumph﴾, meaning: this was only by His grace upon them and His kindness toward them, as is established in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Do deeds, strive, and seek to be near (to perfection), and know that no one's deeds will enter him into Paradise." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even me, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and grace." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6467, from the hadith of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her.]

* *

His saying: ﴿So We have made it easy only in your tongue, that they may remember﴾, meaning: We have made this Qur'an that We revealed easy, clear, evident and plain in your tongue, which is the most eloquent, most manifest, sweetest and most exalted of languages, ﴿that they may remember﴾, meaning: that they may understand and act upon it. Then, since despite this clarity and explicitness some people disbelieved, opposed and were obstinate, Allah (exalted is He) said to His Messenger, consoling him, promising him victory, and warning those who denied him of destruction and ruin: ﴿So wait﴾, meaning: await, ﴿indeed they are waiting﴾, meaning: they will soon know for whom will be the victory, the triumph and the elevation of the word in this world and the Hereafter. Indeed, it is yours, O Muhammad, and your brothers among the prophets and messengers, and those of the believers who follow you, as Allah (exalted is He) said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21], and He (exalted is He) said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand, the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil abode﴾ [Ghafir: 51–52].

End of the commentary on Surah al-Dukhan, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace, and by Him is success and protection.

Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21], and He (exalted is He) said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand, the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil abode﴾ [Ghafir: 51–52].

End of the commentary on Surah al-Dukhan, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace, and by Him is success and protection.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 44, verse 51–59:

When Allah (may He be exalted) mentioned the state of the wretched, He followed it with mention of the state of the blessed (and for this reason the Qur'an is called "al-mathani" [the oft-repeated]). So He said: ﴿Indeed, the righteous [al-muttaqin]﴾, meaning: those who were mindful of Allah in this world, ﴿will be in a secure place﴾, meaning: in the Hereafter, which is Paradise, where they will be safe from death and expulsion, from every worry, sorrow, distress, weariness and fatigue, from Satan and his plotting, and from all other calamities and afflictions.

﴿Among gardens and springs﴾. This is in contrast to what those (the wretched) will have of the tree of zaqqum and the drinking of boiling water.

* *

His saying (exalted is He): ﴿They will wear of fine silk and brocade﴾. Sundus is fine silk, like shirts and the like. ﴿Istabraq﴾ is that which has a sheen and gleam, such as the rich garments and what is worn over the finest fabrics. ﴿Facing one another﴾, meaning: on couches, none of them sitting with his back to another.

* *

His saying: ﴿Thus, and We will pair them with large-eyed houris﴾, meaning: this bounty, along with what We have granted them of wives, the beautiful large-eyed houris, ﴿whom no man or jinn has touched before them﴾ [al-Rahman: 56, 74], ﴿as if they were rubies and coral﴾ [al-Rahman: 58], ﴿Is the reward for good anything but good?﴾ [al-Rahman: 60].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Nuh ibn Habib narrated to us, Nasr ibn Muzahim al-Attar narrated to us, Umar ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from a man, from Anas, (whose narration Nuh raised to the Prophet ﷺ), who said: "If a houri were to spit into a deep sea, that water would become sweet from the sweetness of her saliva." [Abu Nu'aym narrated it in Sifat al-Jannah, no. 386, by another route: from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Hasani, from Mansur al-Wasiti, from Abu al-Nadr al-Abbar, from Anas, raised to the Prophet, with similar wording.]

* *

His saying: ﴿Therein they will call for every kind of fruit, secure﴾, meaning: whatever kinds of fruit they request will be brought to them, and they will be secure that it will not be cut off or withheld, but rather it will come to them whenever they wish.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will not taste death therein, except the first death﴾. This is an exception that emphasizes the negation; it is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), and its meaning is that they will never taste death therein. As is established in the two Sahihs, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Death will be brought in the form of a white-black ram, and it will be stopped between Paradise and Hell, and then it will be slaughtered. Then it will be said: O people of Paradise, eternity, with no death; and O people of Hell, eternity, with no death." The hadith has already been mentioned in the commentary on Surah Maryam [see the takhrij of the hadith at verse 39 of Surah Maryam].

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Muslim al-Agharr, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It will be said to the people of Paradise: Indeed, for you is health, so you will never fall ill; indeed, for you is life, so you will never die; indeed, for you is bounty, so you will never be miserable; indeed, for you is youth, so you will never grow old." Muslim narrated it from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh and Abd ibn Humayd, both from Abd al-Razzaq with the same chain. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2837.]

Thus Abu Ishaq and the people of Iraq say "Abu Muslim al-Agharr," while the people of Medina say "Abu Abd Allah al-Agharr." [The first is the correct one, as Imam al-Mizzi explained in Tahdhib al-Kamal.]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud al-Sijistani said: Ahmad ibn Hafs narrated to us, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from al-Hajjaj — that is, Ibn Hajjaj — from Ubada [in some copies: Qatada], from Ubayd Allah ibn Amr, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever is mindful of Allah enters Paradise, where he will enjoy bounty and will not be miserable, and will live therein and will not die; his garments will not wear out, and his youth will not fade." [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 4895 (Majma' al-Bahrayn), by way of Ahmad ibn Hafs.]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Ubayd Allah al-Raqqi narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Imran ibn al-Rabi' al-Kufi narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ was asked: "Do the people of Paradise sleep?" He said: "Sleep is the brother of death, and the people of Paradise do not sleep." [Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 4875 (Majma' al-Bahrayn); in its chain is Mus'ab ibn Ibrahim al-Absi, who is munkar al-hadith.]

Likewise, Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Sadaqa al-Misri narrated to us, al-Miqdam ibn Dawud narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Sleep is the brother of death, and the people of Paradise do not sleep." [Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilya (7/90), by way of Ahmad ibn al-Qasim from al-Miqdam ibn Dawud, and said: "Gharib from the hadith of al-Thawri; it was narrated solely by Abd Allah."]

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: al-Fadl ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, do the people of Paradise sleep?" He said: "No, sleep is the brother of death." Then he said: "We do not know anyone who transmitted this from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, except al-Thawri, nor from al-Thawri except al-Firyabi." [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3517 (Kashf al-Astar); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/415): "The narrators of al-Bazzar are the narrators of the Sahih."] Thus he said, though the contrary has already been mentioned, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And He protected them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾, meaning: alongside this great, enduring bounty, He has protected them, kept them safe, saved them and distanced them from the painful punishment in the levels of Hell. Thus they have attained what they sought and were delivered from what they feared. For this reason He said: ﴿As a bounty from your Lord. That is the great triumph﴾, meaning: this was only by His grace upon them and His kindness toward them, as is established in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Do deeds, strive, and seek to be near (to perfection), and know that no one's deeds will enter him into Paradise." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even me, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and grace." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6467, from the hadith of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her.]

* *

His saying: ﴿So We have made it easy only in your tongue, that they may remember﴾, meaning: We have made this Qur'an that We revealed easy, clear, evident and plain in your tongue, which is the most eloquent, most manifest, sweetest and most exalted of languages, ﴿that they may remember﴾, meaning: that they may understand and act upon it. Then, since despite this clarity and explicitness some people disbelieved, opposed and were obstinate, Allah (exalted is He) said to His Messenger, consoling him, promising him victory, and warning those who denied him of destruction and ruin: ﴿So wait﴾, meaning: await, ﴿indeed they are waiting﴾, meaning: they will soon know for whom will be the victory, the triumph and the elevation of the word in this world and the Hereafter. Indeed, it is yours, O Muhammad, and your brothers among the prophets and messengers, and those of the believers who follow you, as Allah (exalted is He) said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21], and He (exalted is He) said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand, the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil abode﴾ [Ghafir: 51–52].

End of the commentary on Surah al-Dukhan, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace, and by Him is success and protection.
